subject.title: Cron sessions deliver hallucinated output instead of failing cleanly when tool calls fail

question: What should OpenClaw treat as a fatal finalization failure for unattended cron/session delivery when the turn contains failed, missing, or unattempted tool work but also has final assistant text?
rationale: Current code intentionally allows some recovery after tool warnings, while the issue asks for stronger fail-closed behavior that could suppress legitimate recovered output and has security implications.

options.title: Ledger-backed fail-closed policy
options.body: Require final delivery for unattended runs to be backed by successful required tool calls or explicit typed success evidence, suppressing unsupported success claims after failed or missing tool work.

options.title: Keep current recovery semantics
options.body: Continue treating final assistant text as proof of recovery unless an explicit fatal signal or structured error is present, leaving this issue open only for narrower incidents.

options.title: Cron-only text-marker filter
options.body: Add a narrow cron output filter for self-referential phrases such as mock data or placeholders, accepting that plain unsupported success claims remain possible.

recommendation.title: Ledger-backed fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Require final delivery for unattended runs to be backed by successful required tool calls or explicit typed success evidence, suppressing unsupported success claims after failed or missing tool work.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron finalization behavior in blame is from steipete's recent PR, making him the best available routing owner for the policy question.
